operationName: Ebola PHEIC Response — 2026 Bundibugyo Outbreak, DRC & Uganda
heroHeadline: Ebola Reaches Seventh DRC Province as Toll Hits 6,942 Cases, 3,349 Deaths
heroSubtitle: The 2026 DRC-Uganda Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) outbreak spread to a seventh province — and the first in western DRC — after a 23-year-old man died 9 September in Gwaka, Sud-Ubangi, following a roughly 2,000km, three-week journey through South Kivu, Rwanda, Uganda, Ituri, Tshopo and Mongala; acting Sud-Ubangi Governor Jean-René Galekwa Vundawe said 38 of his contacts have been quarantined. The finding came the same week ECDC's tracker (updated 10 September, data through 9 September) put DRC's confirmed toll at 6,942 cases and 3,349 deaths, a rise of 99 cases and 39 deaths from the prior report, with national contact-tracing coverage slipping to 84.4% from 88.3%. WHO said 10 September that roughly 2,000 frontline and health workers have received the Ervebo vaccine under compassionate use, well short of the 50,000-dose target, while a Phase 3 trial testing Ervebo's cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus remains on track for October or November. The outbreak, per AP, is now tracking toward surpassing the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic's 11,310-death toll.
footerNote: Data sourced from DRC Ministry of Health (MSANTE) situation reports, ECDC outbreak tracker, WHO Disease Outbreak News, Africa CDC statements, Uganda Ministry of Health, CDC Ebola Situation Summary, MSF, AP, AFP, Bloomberg, Al Jazeera, Healio, and UN News. Case counts are rapidly evolving.
